description: Maps each of the 7 interview sections to their target vertex types, edge patterns, extraction goals, and ID conventions. The LLM extractor reads this at session start to scope its output per turn.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.purpose: Establish session identity, scope, and consent. Create the root KnowledgeSession vertex and link the expert Person vertex.
capture_goals: Expert name and role
Specialization and years of experience in hypertension
Session objective and confidentiality level
Expert preferences for pacing or depth
sections.extractor_instruction: Emit the KnowledgeSession vertex first with domain='hypertension'. Then emit the Person vertex and link with hasSession. Do not emit any clinical knowledge nodes in this section.

sections.title: Explicit Clinical Knowledge
sections.purpose: Capture foundational, textbook-verifiable knowledge: classification systems, BP thresholds, diagnostic criteria, signs/symptoms, comorbidities, risk factors, and guideline differences.
capture_goals: Hypertension definition and classification (Stage 1, Stage 2, isolated systolic, etc.)
BP threshold values and measurement context
Diagnostic criteria by guideline (ACC/AHA, ESC, JNC)
Subtle or overlooked signs and symptoms
Comorbidities and their impact on management
Modifiable and non-modifiable risk factors
Guideline differences and expert preference
sections.extractor_instruction: For every classification mentioned (e.g. 'Stage 2 hypertension'), emit one HypertensionConcept vertex. For every BP threshold value, emit one BloodPressureMeasurement vertex and link to its concept with classifiedAs. Attach ProvenanceEvidence to every HypertensionConcept via conceptSupportedBy.

sections.title: Clinical Processes and Workflows
sections.purpose: Capture the expert's step-by-step diagnostic and management workflows: history-taking order, examination priorities, investigation sequencing, when to start medication, follow-up logic, and referral thresholds.
capture_goals: Step-by-step diagnostic process for a new hypertensive patient
Physical exam findings that are often underestimated
Criteria for screening secondary causes
Decision logic: lifestyle-only vs. starting medication
Medication selection and initial dosing approach
Follow-up interval and monitoring items
Criteria for specialist referral
Common protocol exceptions the expert makes
sections.extractor_instruction: Every 'if-then' workflow step becomes a DecisionRule vertex. Link ClinicalFindings that activate rules with triggers. Link medications and lifestyle interventions to the relevant HypertensionConcept. Attach ProvenanceEvidence to every DecisionRule via supportedBy.

sections.title: Experience-Based Insights
sections.purpose: Extract tacit, non-textbook knowledge: heuristics, gut-feeling rules, pattern recognition, subtle cues, common errors, and habits that distinguish experienced clinicians.
capture_goals: Gut-feeling and judgment-call rules
Early warning patterns that predict progression
Difference in feel between typical and atypical presentations
Memorable case that shaped the expert's approach
Most common clinician errors with hypertension
Pitfalls residents fall into
Subtle cues the expert has learned to notice
Habits of seasoned hypertension clinicians
sections.extractor_instruction: Heuristics and gut-feeling rules become ClinicalReasoningPattern vertices. Each mistake or trap becomes a Pitfall vertex linked to the rule it relates to via avoid. If the expert narrates a past case, emit a CaseScenario vertex and link with patternExplainsCase.

sections.title: Case-Based Reasoning
sections.purpose: Extract reasoning through concrete clinical scenarios: newly diagnosed, comorbid diabetes, resistant hypertension, hypertensive emergency, and atypical presentations.
capture_goals: Stage 1 newly diagnosed patient — full reasoning walkthrough
Impact of comorbid diabetes on reasoning and management plan
Approach to resistant hypertension and its pitfalls
Step-by-step management of hypertensive emergency with end-organ damage
IV vs. oral therapy decision logic
Atypical case requiring unconventional thinking
How the expert evaluates competing hypotheses
Balancing guidelines with individual patient context
Re-evaluating assumptions as a case evolves
sections.extractor_instruction: Each scenario the expert walks through becomes one CaseScenario vertex with scenarioType set to the scenario name (e.g. 'resistant_hypertension', 'hypertensive_emergency'). Emit BloodPressureMeasurement for any BP values mentioned and link with hasMeasurement. Emit Outcome for the final disposition and link via leadsTo from the key DecisionRule.

sections.title: Rules, Guidelines, and Decision Criteria
sections.purpose: Capture explicit if-then rules, red flags, hospitalization thresholds, titration logic, contraindications, de-escalation triggers, and risk stratification factors.
capture_goals: Key if-then rules governing management decisions
Red flags requiring urgent or emergent action
BP or clinical thresholds that prompt hospitalization
Medication titration process and decision points
Contraindications that most affect drug selection
Exceptions to standard protocols
Criteria for intensifying therapy
Criteria for de-escalating therapy
Risk stratification factors and weighting
sections.extractor_instruction: Every stated rule — including threshold rules, red flags, and titration steps — becomes a DecisionRule vertex. Set ifCondition and thenAction explicitly. Mark priority as 'urgent' for red-flag rules. Link drug contraindications with contraindicated edges. Reuse existing Medication and Comorbidity vertex IDs — do not duplicate.

sections.title: Contextual and Systemic Factors
sections.purpose: Capture how context modifies clinical decisions: patient preferences, resource constraints, psychosocial barriers, adherence signals, interdisciplinary coordination, and system-level improvement opportunities.
capture_goals: How patient preferences influence care decisions
Adaptations in low-resource or limited-access settings
Psychosocial barriers most affecting adherence
Early signals of likely non-compliance
Role of interdisciplinary coordination in hypertension care
System-level changes that would most improve outcomes
sections.extractor_instruction: For each context-dependent modification (e.g. 'in low-resource settings I avoid X'), emit one ContextualConstraint vertex and link to the relevant DecisionRule with modulatedBy, or to FollowUpPlan with constraintModulatesPlan. Reuse DecisionRule and FollowUpPlan IDs from prior sections — do not duplicate. This section enriches existing nodes, not create new clinical concepts.

global_extractor_rules.vertex_reuse: Always check the known vertex ID cache before emitting a new vertex. If the same concept was extracted in a prior section, add edges to the existing vertex — never duplicate.
global_extractor_rules.provenance_required: Every extracted knowledge vertex (not session/transcript infrastructure) must have at least one outgoing supportedBy or conceptSupportedBy edge to a ProvenanceEvidence node in the same delta.
global_extractor_rules.one_delta_per_turn: Emit one delta per conversational turn. Do not batch multiple turns into one delta.
global_extractor_rules.id_format: All IDs are lowercase, hyphen-separated slugs. No spaces, no special characters.
global_extractor_rules.session_root_first: KnowledgeSession must be written to the graph before any other vertex in Section A. The extractor must not emit downstream vertices if the session root write fails.
